result.scope_note: The claim compares body byte payloads between two HTTP status/operation pairs (GET vs HEAD) for identical nonempty resources, governed by the HTTP/1.1 specification (RFC 9110/9112) as of 2022. Per that standard, a 200 GET response always includes the full representation body, while a 200 HEAD response MUST NOT include a message body; it returns only header fields. Therefore, for any nonempty resource, the GET response carries strictly more body bytes (in fact, HEAD carries zero bytes). This holds worldwide under the 2022 standard.
